subject: Request: Structured remediation grant for Hearthlytics — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Sarah Mills <sarah@hearthlytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service disruption impact — Hearthlytics (May 29–30)

Jonas —

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. To recap, Hearthlytics saw sustained 5–15% elevated error rates across our inference routes between 2026-05-29 13:20 PDT and 2026-05-30 02:05 PDT. That window caused failed recommendations for ~18% of active requests and materially affected our nightly billing/job runs. Our ops team logged multiple retries and several downstream jobs had to be re-run manually.

We need a remediation proposal from Redwood: a clear breakdown of the outage cause, an estimate of the customer impact (token counts / failed request volume), and a proposal for service remediation or account-level compensation. Our procurement and finance teams will need something concrete to process any credits or contract amendments.

Please include an itemised remediation plan and proposed timeline — we are aiming to finalize this week.

— Sarah
Sarah Mills
Head of Platform 
Hearthlytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah@hearthlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:04:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption impact — Hearthlytics (May 29–30)

Hi Sarah —

First, really sorry for the disruption and for the additional operational work your team had to do. We own this and want to make it right quickly. I attached a short uptime analysis and a proposed remediation grant structure for your review (uptime-analysis-june-01.pdf, proposed-remediation-grant.csv).

High level summary:
- Root cause: an overloaded routing tier that failed to fallback cleanly to the cheaper model shard under sustained tail latency.
- Customer impact (prelim): ~1.2M tokens attempted, ~210k attempts that experienced elevated failures or retries.
- Proposed immediate gesture (draft):
  1) Immediate invoice-level credit equal to 25% of May usage for impacted routes (applied to next invoice).
  2) One-time engineering fund credit of $20,000 to cover incident remediation & support hours (applied within 90 days).
  3) 30-day service extension (no charge) to offset operational disruption to scheduled jobs.

This structure is meant to be a balanced remedy that addresses both the quantitative impact and the operational overhead Hearthlytics incurred. Because it exceeds standard credit bands for our self-serve plans, I need executive approval to commit to 2) and 3) as written.

If this looks reasonable I will ask for a quick approval from Finance/Leadership and route the amended order form and legal addendum. Happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: uptime-analysis-june-01.pdf, proposed-remediation-grant.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 08:22:45 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Service disruption impact — Hearthlytics (ask: exec approval for remediation grant)

Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Hearthlytics' note and the remediation proposal I shared. They accepted the concept but want final signoff this week so procurement can process an amended order. Key items for approval:

Proposed remediation grant (recommended):
- Tranche A (immediate): 25% credit on May invoice for impacted routes — applied to next invoice.
- Tranche B (engineering fund): one-time $20,000 credit to be used to cover Redwood support/engineering hours or applied as a bill credit if unused — expires in 90 days.
- Tranche C (goodwill extension): 30 days of free service (pause of billing on their primary production route) — applied as a calendar extension on the contract.

Rationale:
- Compensates both measurable token loss and the manual remediation work Hearthlytics performed.
- Structured so we limit ongoing revenue leakage (one-time credits + time-limited extension).
- Matches similar escalations we've granted, but the engineering fund is slightly higher because of the operational re-runs.

Risks / considerations:
- Precedent: we should mark this as a one-off settlement for this account and require a formal sign-off from Legal to amend the order form.
- Accounting: Finance will need a memo; this will be processed as contra-revenue for May.

Attachments: impact-log-may29-30.txt, proposed-remediation-grant.csv

Ask: Laura — can you authorize the remediation grant as described, or suggest modifications? If approved, I'll prepare the amended OF and run the DocuSign flow.

Thanks,
Jonas
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Mills <sarah@hearthlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 16:40:03 -0700
Subject: Approval: Hearthlytics remediation grant (conditional)

Team —

Thanks for the clear summary. I reviewed the incident notes and the proposed grant. I approve a modified remediation package on the conditions below:

Approved package (final):
- Tranche A: 25% invoice credit for May on impacted routes — approved as-is.
- Tranche B: one-time engineering fund credit reduced to $15,000 (approved).
- Tranche C: 14-day goodwill service extension (approved) instead of 30 days.

Conditions / next steps:
1) Mark this as a non-precedent, one-off settlement and include language in the amendment that it is a goodwill, non-recurring concession.
2) Legal to review and approve amended order form. Please loop in Legal (legal@redwood.com) before DocuSign.
3) Finance to process as contra-revenue for May and prepare the credit memo.
4) Ops to provide a short postmortem (1–2 pages) capturing root cause and remediation actions; copy to customer ops team within 7 business days.

Jonas — proceed to prepare the amendment and coordinate Legal/Finance. Sarah — we'll issue the credit and the engineering fund as a billing credit; Legal will send a short amendment for signature.

Laura Bennett
SVP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
